{
"Reactive Programming": "A declarative programming paradigm centered on asynchronous data streams and the automatic propagation of changes through a system. It enables building responsive, event-driven applications by composing operations over streams of values.",
"Data Stream": "A sequence of data elements made available over time, which can be processed incrementally rather than as a complete dataset. It serves as the fundamental abstraction for handling asynchronous data flows in reactive systems.",
"Propagation of Changes": "The mechanism by which updates to a data source are automatically forwarded through dependent computations and subscribers. It ensures that derived values and observers remain consistent with their underlying sources without manual intervention.",
"Observable": "A reactive abstraction representing a push-based data source that emits a sequence of values, errors, or completion signals to its subscribers over time. It is the primary producer entity in reactive programming.",
"Data Source": "An origin that produces data values, events, or signals which can be consumed by downstream components. In reactive systems, data sources are typically wrapped as observables to enable stream-based processing.",
"Stream": "An ordered, potentially unbounded sequence of asynchronous events or values flowing between producers and consumers. Streams form the core conduit through which reactive data moves and is transformed.",
"Asynchronous Event": "A discrete occurrence or value emitted at an unpredictable point in time, independent of the consumer's execution flow. Such events are the fundamental units carried by reactive streams.",
"Operator": "A function that takes one or more streams as input and returns a transformed stream, enabling composition of reactive pipelines. Operators encapsulate reusable behaviors such as filtering, mapping, combining, or aggregating events.",
"Map Operator": "An operator that applies a transformation function to each emitted value of a stream, producing a new stream of transformed values. It preserves the ordering and cardinality of the original emissions.",
"Filter Operator": "An operator that emits only those values from a source stream which satisfy a specified predicate, discarding the rest. It is used to selectively narrow a stream to relevant events.",
"FlatMap Operator": "An operator that maps each emission of a source stream to an inner observable and flattens the resulting observables into a single output stream. It is used for composing asynchronous operations and handling nested streams.",
"Subscription": "A connection established between an observer and an observable that initiates the flow of emissions and can be used to cancel it. It represents the lifecycle of a consumer's interest in a stream.",
"Observer": "An entity that consumes the values, errors, and completion notifications emitted by an observable. Observers define the reactions to be executed in response to each type of signal received.",
"Backpressure": "A flow-control mechanism that allows consumers to signal their processing capacity to producers, preventing overload when emissions outpace consumption. It is essential for building stable reactive systems under varying load.",
"Consumer": "A component that receives and processes values from a stream or observable. Consumers may apply backpressure strategies to regulate how quickly they ingest emitted data.",
"Emission Rate": "The frequency at which an observable or stream produces values over time. Managing this rate is critical to ensuring that downstream consumers can keep up without buffering excessively or dropping data."
}
